priority.override_reason: Ranks 1 through 6 are closed by current rejected direct-leaf frame, constructor, heap-value-cache, direct-eval, and RegExp evidence. The current rank-7 SHA-256 profile and exact bytecode inspection identify a distinct structural blocker: its 64-round numeric loop is otherwise admitted by the existing shape-independent typed-loop executor, but a dense local Array write whose key is an arithmetic expression cannot be lowered. The proposed admission is defined only by bytecode shape, compiler-temporary ownership, and existing runtime array guards; it has no workload, source-path, checksum, or iteration-count condition.

mechanism.summary: Extend the existing typed-loop element-assignment lowering so an existing dense local Array may use a prevalidated scalar index expression, rather than requiring the key to be one raw local-slot load, before its value expression and existing DenseWrite operation.
mechanism.generality: The extension applies to every compiler-emitted receiver/key/value temporary sequence whose receiver is a local Array, whose index and value subexpressions are already admitted by the typed-loop scalar program, and whose temporary slots are compiler-owned and unread outside the region. The same live dense-array, in-bounds, writable-element, numeric-index, alias, and deoptimization guards remain authoritative. Branching subexpressions, observable property receivers, non-integer or non-Number keys, holes, growth, indexed descriptors, frozen arrays, stale temporary ownership, direct eval, and any unsupported bytecode retain the existing interpreter path.
semantic_risks: the receiver must be captured before the index and value exactly once, and the generated register program must preserve JavaScript evaluation order
an index expression that leaves the scalar domain must deopt at the exact instruction with the operand stack and completed writes restored
only compiler-generated temporaries that have no observable reads outside the region may be elided; user-visible assignments and completion values must retain their existing writeback semantics
dense writes must retain existing bounds, holes, descriptors, frozen-array, alias, and replay behavior rather than assuming the Array stays ordinary

profile_evidence.source: macOS sample 2026-07-27 /private/tmp/qjs-profile-sha256-current-1e534.sample; 20x hash-verified Kraken stanford-crypto-sha256-iterative direct-script bundle executed by the exact 1e534 candidate binary, followed by exact bytecode inspection of its 64-round compression loop
profile_evidence.shared_cost: The 2,934-sample profile is dominated by Vm::run_completion with repeated eval_binary and fast_number_binary chains. The exact 207-op compression-loop bytecode has admitted scalar control flow and dense reads, but compilation stops at the generic SetProp form generated for a local dense-array write with key `counter & 15`; this forces every one of the 64 rounds through ordinary operand-stack and Value dispatch.
